subject: Money
title: The Deflation Trap
description: A 60-second lesson on The Deflation Trap.

hook.text: If prices drop 2% per year, why buy a TV today when it's cheaper tomorrow? Everyone waits. Nobody spends.

buildup.text: Deflation means falling prices. It sounds good but destroys economies. Spending freezes, businesses fail, jobs vanish.

discovery.text: When prices fall, debt becomes heavier in real terms. A $100,000 mortgage buys more each year—crushing borrowers.

twist.text: Deflation is harder to escape than inflation. You can raise rates to kill inflation, but rates can't go below zero.

climax.text: Japan battled deflation for 30 years. Despite trillions in stimulus, prices barely moved. The trap is real.

punchline.text: Falling prices sound great. The economy disagrees.

quiz.question: Why is deflation dangerous for borrowers?
options: Debt becomes heavier in real terms as prices fall
